name: Hotel Druk, Phuentsholing
summary: A long-running certified 3-star hotel on Zhung Lam, about 100 m from the Bhutan Gate. It is the practical first night of a road trip: walk to immigration, eat on the main street and leave early for Thimphu.
body: Hotel Druk sits on Zhung Lam, Phuentsholing's main street, roughly 100 m from the gate that divides the town from Jaigaon. It belongs to the Druk Hotels group, which also runs the Hotel Druk in Thimphu, and is a Department of Tourism-certified 3-star property, so it meets the rule that tourists must stay in certified hotels. Rooms are plain and clean, with air conditioning, which matters in a town that passes 35 °C in summer.

The location is the reason to stay. You can walk to the pedestrian terminal for your entry permit, to the banks and to the restaurants on the main street, and leave early for the 5–6 hour drive to Thimphu without crossing town. The in-house restaurant serves Indian, Chinese and Bhutanese food. On the way out of Bhutan it also works as a last night before the drive back to Siliguri or Bagdogra.
why: About 100 m from the Bhutan Gate and immigration
Certified 3-star, so valid for tourist itineraries
Air conditioning for Phuentsholing's heat
watch_out: Rooms facing Zhung Lam can hear street and border traffic in the evening; ask for a room at the back.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Druk from the Phuentsholing border gate
faqs.a: About 100 m along Zhung Lam, a two-minute walk. That makes it easy to reach the pedestrian terminal for your entry permit and to cross back to Jaigaon if you need to. Cars can drop you at the door. It is one of the most central hotels in Phuentsholing.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Druk Phuentsholing a certified hotel for tourists
faqs.a: Yes. It is listed as a Department of Tourism-certified 3-star hotel, which tourists, including Indian nationals, are required to use in Bhutan. Your tour operator can include it in the itinerary submitted for the entry permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What does a room at Hotel Druk Phuentsholing cost
faqs.a: Roughly ₹3,500–5,500 per room night with breakfast, indicative 2026, depending on season and room type. Rates rise during Durga Puja, Diwali and the December holidays, when Indian tourists cross in large numbers. Book a few weeks ahead for those dates.

name: Hotel Olathang
summary: One of Bhutan's oldest hotels, built in 1974 for guests at the Fourth King's coronation, set in about 28 acres of blue pine on a hill above Paro. Traditional buildings, cottages and a spa with hot stone baths, at a mid-range price.
body: Hotel Olathang opened in 1974 to house the foreign guests invited to the coronation of the Fourth King, Jigme Singye Wangchuck, when Bhutan had almost no hotels. It stands on a hill about 5 km above Paro town, in some 28 acres of blue pine forest, with a main building around a courtyard and cottage rooms scattered through the grounds. The architecture is traditional Bhutanese, with painted woodwork and sloping roofs.

Rooms are comfortable rather than modern, which is part of the appeal and the price. The restaurant serves Bhutanese, Indian, Chinese and Continental food, and the Dewa Spa offers the Bhutanese hot stone bath, massage and a sauna. From the grounds you look down over the Paro valley and airport. It is a good base for the Tiger's Nest hike, 20–30 minutes away by car, and for the drive over Chele La to Haa.
why: Built for the 1974 coronation; real Bhutanese history
Pine-forest setting with valley views
Hot stone bath in the hotel spa
watch_out: Some older rooms show their age and heating varies by block; ask for a renovated room or a cottage in winter.

faqs.q: When was Hotel Olathang built
faqs.a: In 1974, to accommodate foreign guests at the coronation of the Fourth King, Jigme Singye Wangchuck. That makes it one of the oldest hotels in Bhutan. It has been extended since with cottage rooms in the surrounding pine forest above Paro.

faqs.q: How far is Hotel Olathang from Paro town and the airport
faqs.a: It is on a hill about 5 km from Paro town, roughly 10–15 minutes by car, and a similar distance from Paro airport. The Tiger's Nest trailhead is about 20–30 minutes away. You will need your car to go into town for dinner.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Olathang have a hot stone bath
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel's Dewa Spa offers the traditional Bhutanese hot stone bath along with massage, sauna and steam. Book it a few hours ahead so the stones can be heated. It is a good way to end the Tiger's Nest day; prices are higher than at a farmhouse.

name: Hotel Lobesa
summary: A small certified 3-star hotel at Lobesa, on the slope between Chimi Lhakhang and the Punakha valley, with around a dozen rooms and balconies over the rice fields. Good value for a two-night Punakha stay.
body: Hotel Lobesa is a small, three-star hotel at Lobesa, the junction where the road from Thimphu splits towards Punakha and Wangdue. It has about 13 rooms, most with balconies looking over the terraced fields and the valley. Its size keeps it quiet and the staff attentive. The restaurant serves Bhutanese dishes, Indian food on request and simple Continental options.

The location suits a Punakha itinerary well. Chimi Lhakhang is a short drive and a 20-minute field walk away, Punakha Dzong is about 20–25 minutes by car, and Wangdue Phodrang is close for the drive to Phobjikha. Because Punakha is low and warm, rooms are comfortable in winter without heavy heating. It is a sensible budget choice for couples and small families.
why: Balcony rooms over the Punakha rice terraces
Close to Chimi Lhakhang and the Wangdue road
Small and quiet
watch_out: With only about 13 rooms it fills early in festival weeks and cannot take large groups together.

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Lobesa in Punakha
faqs.a: At Lobesa, where the Thimphu road divides towards Punakha and Wangdue, about 20–25 minutes by car from Punakha Dzong. Chimi Lhakhang is close by. The hotel sits on the slope with views over the rice terraces of the lower valley.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Lobesa good for budget travellers
faqs.a: Yes. It is a certified 3-star hotel at roughly ₹3,500–5,500 per room night with breakfast, indicative 2026, which is at the lower end for Punakha. Rooms are simple but clean with balconies. Book early in February–March, when the Punakha festivals fill the valley.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Lobesa serve vegetarian food
faqs.a: Yes. Bhutanese cooking has many vegetarian dishes, such as ema datshi, kewa datshi and red rice, and the kitchen can prepare Indian vegetarian food on request. Tell your guide or the hotel in advance about any dietary needs, including Jain or no-onion requirements.

name: Hotel Druk, Thimphu
image_query: Hotel Druk Thimphu Clock Tower Square
summary: A central hotel on Thimphu's Clock Tower Square, part of the Druk Hotels group. You can walk to cafes, the craft bazaar and Norzin Lam, and the rooms are heated properly for Thimphu's cold winters.
body: Hotel Druk faces the Clock Tower Square, the open plaza at the heart of Thimphu where events and concerts are held. It is one of the city's established mid-range hotels and belongs to the same group as the Hotel Druk in Phuentsholing. Rooms are comfortable, with central heating, which counts in a city where winter nights drop below freezing. The hotel has a restaurant serving Indian, Bhutanese and Continental food.

Its strength is location. Norzin Lam, the main street, is a minute away, with cafes, bookshops and the handicraft emporiums. The weekend market and the Memorial Chorten are short drives or a 15–20 minute walk. In the evening you can stroll around the square and the town without needing the car. It suits families and older travellers who want comfort without the price of Thimphu's premium hotels.
why: On the Clock Tower Square, walkable to Norzin Lam
Proper heating for Thimphu winters
Reliable mid-range comfort
watch_out: Events on the Clock Tower Square can be noisy into the evening; ask for a room away from the square if you sleep early.

faqs.q: Where is Hotel Druk in Thimphu
faqs.a: On the Clock Tower Square in central Thimphu, a minute from Norzin Lam, the main street. Cafes, shops and the craft bazaar are within walking distance, and Tashichho Dzong, the Memorial Chorten and the weekend market are short drives. It is one of the most central hotels in the city.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Druk Thimphu good for families
faqs.a: Yes. Rooms are spacious and heated, the restaurant offers Indian and Bhutanese food, and the central location means children can walk around the square in the evening. Ask for connecting or family rooms when booking. It sits in our comfort tier at roughly ₹7,000–12,000 per room night, indicative 2026.

faqs.q: Does Hotel Druk Thimphu have heating in winter
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel has central heating, which matters in Thimphu from November to February, when night temperatures drop below 0 °C. Ask for an extra blanket if you feel the cold. Budget hotels in Thimphu often rely on small room heaters instead.

name: Dhensa Boutique Resort
summary: A small resort of six cottages and 24 rooms on a pine-covered hillside above the Punakha river at Wolakha, with balconies, a glass-walled dining room and a spa with an outdoor wood-fired bath. Our pick for comfortable couples' stays in Punakha.
body: Dhensa sits on a mountainside at Wolakha, above the Punakha valley, among pine forest with walking trails around it. It has 24 rooms in six cottages, each room with a private balcony looking over the river and rice fields. Rooms have air conditioning and heating, Wi-Fi and the comforts of a good boutique hotel. The dining room is glass-walled, with a stone terrace outside for meals in the sun.

The kitchen uses local, seasonal produce and serves Bhutanese, Asian and Western dishes. The Kibu Spa offers massage, yoga, a sauna and steam room and an outdoor wood-fired bath. It works well as a quiet base for two nights: Punakha Dzong and Chimi Lhakhang are within about 30 minutes, and you return each evening to a hillside that feels far from the road.
why: Balconies over the Punakha valley from every room
Spa with an outdoor wood-fired bath
Small and quiet, among pine forest
watch_out: It is a drive from the dzong and town, so you depend on your car for every outing, and paths between cottages involve some steps.

faqs.q: Is Dhensa Boutique Resort good for a honeymoon
faqs.a: Yes. It is small, quiet and set on a forested hillside above the valley, with balconies on every room, a glass-walled dining room and a spa with an outdoor wood-fired bath. Rates are roughly ₹15,000–25,000 per room night, indicative 2026, which places it between budget hotels and Punakha's luxury lodges.

faqs.q: How far is Dhensa from Punakha Dzong
faqs.a: About 20–30 minutes by car, depending on traffic and where you stop. The resort is on the hillside at Wolakha above the Punakha river. You will need your car and guide to reach the dzong, Chimi Lhakhang and the suspension bridge.

faqs.q: Does Dhensa Resort have a spa
faqs.a: Yes, the Kibu Spa, with massage, yoga, a sauna and steam room and an outdoor wood-fired bath. Book treatments at check-in, especially in busy months. The outdoor bath is most pleasant on cool evenings from October to March.

name: Dewachen Hotel
summary: A comfortable hotel on the slope of the Phobjikha valley, about 3 km from Gangtey Goenpa, with wood-stove rooms, picture windows over the crane marsh and a restaurant built around a central stove. Ideal for crane season.
body: Dewachen stands at the edge of the Phobjikha valley, close to the Black Mountains National Park and about 3 km from Gangtey Goenpa. The building is traditional in style, and the rooms are heated with wood-burning stoves, with hot water bottles supplied on cold nights. Picture windows, and in many rooms balconies, face out over the valley, so in winter you can see the cranes' feeding grounds from your room.

The restaurant has a central stove and wide windows on the valley, and serves Bhutanese and international food. There is a bar, a hot stone bath and a small gift shop. Staff can arrange walks, horse riding and visits to the monastery and the crane information centre. It is the comfortable middle choice in a valley where the alternatives are simple farmhouses or the expensive Gangtey Lodge and Amankora.
why: Wood-stove rooms with valley views
Close to the crane feeding grounds
Hot stone bath on site
watch_out: Wood-stove heating dies down by early morning in midwinter, and the valley can have power cuts; pack thermals and a torch.

faqs.q: Can you see the cranes from Dewachen Hotel
faqs.a: Often, yes. The hotel faces the Phobjikha valley and its marsh, where the black-necked cranes feed from November to mid-February, so many rooms and the restaurant have a view over their grounds. Binoculars help. For close watching, go to the crane information centre or the road edge at dawn.

faqs.q: Is Dewachen Hotel warm in winter
faqs.a: Rooms are heated with wood-burning stoves and hot water bottles are provided, which keeps them comfortable in the evening. By early morning the stove burns low and nights outside fall to −5 °C or lower, so pack thermals. Ask staff to relight the stove if needed.

faqs.q: How far is Dewachen Hotel from Gangtey Monastery
faqs.a: About 3 km, a few minutes by car or a pleasant 45-minute walk. The Gangtey nature trail and the Black-necked Crane Information Centre are also close. The hotel is on the valley slope near the Black Mountains National Park boundary.

name: Taj Tashi
summary: Thimphu's best-known luxury hotel, built in dzong style a few minutes' walk from the city centre and close to Tashichho Dzong. Large heated rooms with painted woodwork, a spa and the city at the door.
body: Taj Tashi was built in the style of a dzong, with whitewashed walls, sloping roofs and painted wooden windows, and the interiors carry hand-painted murals and Bhutanese textiles. It stands on the edge of central Thimphu, so you can walk to Norzin Lam, the cafes and the craft bazaar, and Tashichho Dzong is a short drive. Rooms are large, well heated and have views over the city or the hills.

The hotel has several restaurants, including Indian and Bhutanese menus, a bar, a spa and a fitness centre. Service is polished in the way Taj guests from India will recognise. It suits travellers who want luxury in the capital without going out of town, and who value a central base over a remote lodge. For families celebrating a special occasion, it is also an easier choice than the small, quiet luxury lodges in Paro and Punakha.
why: Dzong-style building with hand-painted interiors
Walking distance to central Thimphu
Familiar Taj service and Indian food
watch_out: It is a city hotel; if you want silence and valley views, Paro and Punakha lodges do that better.

faqs.q: Is Taj Tashi in central Thimphu
faqs.a: Yes. It is on the edge of the city centre, a short walk from Norzin Lam and the cafes, and a few minutes' drive from Tashichho Dzong. That makes it the most central of Thimphu's luxury hotels. You can go out on foot in the evening without your car.

faqs.q: How much does Taj Tashi cost per night
faqs.a: Roughly ₹25,000–45,000 per room night, indicative 2026, depending on room type, season and offers. Remember that the SDF of ₹1,200 per person per night for Indians, or US$100 for other nationalities, is paid separately on top of the hotel bill. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does Taj Tashi serve Indian food
faqs.a: Yes. Its restaurants include Indian dishes alongside Bhutanese and international menus, and the kitchen handles vegetarian and Jain requests. It is a comfortable choice for Indian families who want familiar food after days of datshi and red rice.

name: COMO Uma Paro
summary: A luxury lodge on a forested ridge above the Paro valley, with rooms and private villas, a spa known for its holistic treatments and Bhutanese and international cooking. A quiet base for the Tiger's Nest and the end of a trip.
body: COMO Uma Paro stands in pine forest on a ridge above Paro town, looking across the valley. It has rooms in the main lodge and private villas, finished in pale wood and Bhutanese textiles. The setting is quiet: you hear wind in the pines and see the lights of Paro below at night. The airport is about 15 minutes away, and the Tiger's Nest trailhead about 20–30 minutes.

The lodge is known for its spa, which offers massage, yoga and hot stone baths, and for its kitchen, which serves Bhutanese dishes alongside lighter international food. Guides can arrange hikes, archery and farmhouse visits. It is one of the best places in Bhutan to rest after the Tiger's Nest hike or before an early flight. COMO also runs a sister lodge in Punakha, so couples often combine the two.
why: Ridge-top setting above the Paro valley
Spa with hot stone baths and yoga
Close to the airport and Tiger's Nest
watch_out: Prices are high and the SDF is extra; the lodge is a drive from Paro town, so you rely on the hotel or your car.

faqs.q: How far is COMO Uma Paro from Paro airport
faqs.a: About 15 minutes by car. The lodge sits on a forested ridge above Paro town, which also puts the Tiger's Nest trailhead about 20–30 minutes away. It is a convenient last night before a morning flight out of Paro.

faqs.q: Is COMO Uma Paro worth it for a honeymoon
faqs.a: For couples with the budget, yes: quiet ridge-top villas, a respected spa and good food. Rates are roughly ₹45,000–80,000 per room night, indicative 2026, with the SDF extra at ₹1,200 per person per night for Indians or US$100 for other nationalities. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does COMO Uma Paro offer a hot stone bath
faqs.a: Yes. The spa offers the Bhutanese hot stone bath. Book in advance so the stones can be heated. It is a more polished version of the farmhouse bath, at a higher price, and pairs well with the Tiger's Nest day.

name: Gangtey Lodge
summary: A small luxury lodge of 12 suites just below Gangtey Goenpa, with fireplaces, roll-top baths and wide windows over the Phobjikha valley. The finest place to watch the cranes from your room.
body: Gangtey Lodge sits on the slope just below Gangtey Goenpa, looking across the whole of the Phobjikha valley. It has 12 suites, each with a fireplace, a roll-top bath and floor-to-ceiling windows on the valley. The design mixes Bhutanese farmhouse style with modern comfort. It is a member of Small Luxury Hotels of the World. In crane season you can watch the birds on the marsh from your room or the terrace.

Meals are served in a main lodge with a central fireplace and long tables, and stays are usually on a full-board basis with activities. Staff arrange walks on the Gangtey nature trail, visits to the monastery and farmhouses, and crane watching with guides. The lodge has a spa with hot stone baths. It suits couples and families who want the valley's quiet and the cranes with every comfort, and who can accept the price.
why: Suites with fireplaces and valley windows
Just below Gangtey Goenpa
Crane watching from the terrace in winter
watch_out: It is one of the most expensive stays in Bhutan and books out early for November–February; the valley is very cold at night.

faqs.q: How many rooms does Gangtey Lodge have
faqs.a: Twelve suites, each with a fireplace, a roll-top bath and wide windows over the Phobjikha valley. The small size keeps it quiet and personal. Book several months ahead for the crane season from November to February, when it fills first.

faqs.q: Can you see black-necked cranes from Gangtey Lodge
faqs.a: Yes, in season. The lodge looks over the marsh where the cranes feed from November to mid-February, and staff arrange guided crane watching at dawn and dusk. A pair of binoculars in your bag helps. Outside the season, the valley is quiet farmland and forest.

faqs.q: What does Gangtey Lodge cost
faqs.a: Roughly ₹60,000–1,00,000 per room night, indicative 2026, typically including meals and some activities. The SDF is paid separately: ₹1,200 per person per night for Indians, US$100 for other nationalities. Check current rates and status with the lodge before you travel.
